title: Seaplane Insurance: Floats, Amphibians, Water Landings and the Costs Land Pilots Never See
description: Seaplane insurance explained: float vs amphibian pricing, SES experience underwriters want, wreck-removal costs, mooring gaps and 5–10% hull deductibles.
author: Insurance Bhaiya Research Desk
keyTakeaways: Underwriters weigh **seaplane time** above everything else, then time in type, amphibian time (if insuring an amphib) and total time.
**Amphibians cost more to insure than straight floats** because retractable gear adds the risk of a gear-down water landing, which often flips the aircraft.
Hull deductibles on seaplanes commonly run **5%–10% of hull value**, and floats are typically covered as a separately scheduled part of physical damage.
Wreck removal can cost **tens of thousands of dollars** and may be legally required whatever the salvage value. Confirm that your policy has a dedicated limit for it.

faqs.question: Is seaplane insurance more expensive than regular airplane insurance?
faqs.answer: Generally yes. Water operations, wreck-removal exposure and the gear risk on amphibians push hull pricing and deductibles above the same airframe on wheels. Seaplane-specific time is the biggest discount lever. See the [aircraft & aviation insurance explained](/learn/aircraft-aviation-insurance-explained/) hub for the fundamentals.

faqs.question: Are floats covered under hull insurance?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, as a separately scheduled part of physical damage cover, for example $50,000 of a $300,000 hull value. Confirm that float theft is included.

faqs.question: Does seaplane insurance cover damage while the plane is docked?
faqs.answer: Not-in-motion cover usually applies, but wind and wave damage to docked or beached seaplanes can be limited depending on the policy wording. Ask your broker to confirm in writing.

content.text: Seaplane insurance covers the same two building blocks as any aircraft policy, hull and liability, but water changes how losses happen and how much they cost. A sunk airframe has to be recovered from the lake bed, a docked floatplane can be wrecked by a storm without ever moving, and a single gear-position error can flip an amphibian on landing. This is a spoke of our [aircraft & aviation insurance explained](/learn/aircraft-aviation-insurance-explained/) hub.
What Underwriters Look At Before Quoting a Seaplane

items: **Seaplane (SES) time:** The most important factor. A 2,000-hour land pilot with 10 hours on floats is still a low-time seaplane pilot.

**Time in type:** Hours in the specific make and model, such as a Cessna 185 on floats or a Super Cub on amphibs. Cessna airframes on floats follow the same logic as our [Cessna insurance](/qa/cessna-insurance/) pricing, but with water-operation loadings added.
**Amphibian time:** Required separately if you're insuring an amphibian, because gear management is the key risk.
**Total time, ratings and recurrent training:** Seaplane-specific recurrent training is viewed favorably.

content.text: Straight Floats vs Amphibians: Why the Gear Matters

Straight floats only operate from water, so the pilot never has to manage landing gear. Amphibious floats add retractable wheels so the aircraft can use runways too. The trade-off is the risk of landing on water with the wheels down, which typically flips the aircraft, or landing on a runway with them up. Amphibious gear is also expensive to repair. As a result, amphibians are priced higher than the same airframe on straight floats, and insurers may require amphibian-specific dual instruction.

content.title: Wreck Removal Can Cost More Than the Airplane Is Worth
content.text: Raising a sunk floatplane can cost tens of thousands of dollars, and authorities can require removal whatever the aircraft's salvage value. Check that your policy has a wreck-removal or salvage limit separate from the hull value. Otherwise, a total loss can leave you paying for the recovery yourself. Boat owners face the same issue. See [boat insurance claims: what to expect](/learn/boat-insurance-claims-what-to-expect/).
Docked, Moored and Beached: The Not-in-Motion Gap

Standard not-in-motion hull cover was written with hangars and tie-downs in mind. Depending on the policy wording, damage from wind or waves to a **docked or beached seaplane** may be limited or excluded, and some policies exclude superficial hail damage that doesn't affect airworthiness. Read the wording carefully, using our guide to [what an exclusion is in insurance](/learn/what-is-an-exclusion-in-insurance/). If you swap between wheels and floats seasonally, some policies require the change to be scheduled with the insurer in advance.

rows: Upgrade to smooth limits if you carry passengers. See [smooth vs per-seat](/compare/smooth-liability-vs-per-seat-sublimit-aircraft-insurance/)

content.text: With a 5%–10% deductible, a $200,000 floatplane leaves you responsible for the first $10,000–$20,000 of any hull loss. That [deductible](/glossary/deductible/) has to sit in your emergency fund, not on a credit card. For general premium context, see [airplane insurance cost](/learn/airplane-insurance-cost/). If you're building a float-equipped kitplane, also read [experimental aircraft insurance](/learn/experimental-aircraft-insurance/).

content.title: Get Your Rating on a Rented Floatplane First
content.text: Most pilots earn the SES rating in a school's floatplane. Carry [private pilot insurance](/qa/private-pilot-insurance/) that explicitly covers non-owned seaplanes, because some renter policies exclude amphibians or water operations. Then build hours before buying. Our [first-airplane scenario](/scenarios/brian-first-cessna-182-texas/) shows how hours in type move a quote.

If the worst happens on the water, follow the NTSB and insurer steps in [aircraft insurance claims: what to expect](/learn/aircraft-insurance-claims-what-to-expect/), and confirm the wreck-removal limit before you call a salvage company. Float operations also raise aviation flat extras on life insurance (see [does life insurance cover private pilots](/qa/does-life-insurance-cover-private-pilots/)). Instructors giving SES training need their own cover, explained in [flight instructor insurance](/qa/flight-instructor-insurance/). Docked-aircraft gaps are explained further in [what does aircraft hull insurance cover](/qa/what-does-aircraft-hull-insurance-cover/).
